summary: The lecture concludes the Vedic Civilization series with a comparative analysis of Early (1500–1000 BCE) and Later (1000–600 BCE) Vedic periods across social, political, and religious spheres. It details the eight forms of marriage, distinguishing sanctioned (Brahma, Prajapatya, Daiva, Arsha, Gandharva) from unsanctioned (Asura, Rakshasa, Paishacha) types, and explains Anuloma and Pratiloma rules. Key societal shifts include the decline of women's status, rigidification of the varna system, and the transition from cattle to land as primary wealth. Religious evolution moves from nature gods (Indra, Agni, Soma) and animism to the trinity (Brahma, Rudra, Vishnu), elaborate sacrifices, and belief in afterlife.
points: Vedic period: 1500–600 BCE; Early (Rigvedic) 1500–1000 BCE, Later 1000–600 BCE.

Eight marriages: Brahma (dowry), Prajapatya (no dowry), Daiva (to priest), Arsha (bride price: cow+bull), Gandharva (love), Asura (purchase), Rakshasa (capture), Paishacha (seduction); first five sanctioned.
Anuloma: groom higher caste, bride same/lower; Pratiloma: bride higher caste, groom same/lower.
Stridhan: woman's exclusive property (gifts, jewelry, land) for economic security; existed since Vedic period.
Early Vedic: no Sati, no child marriage; women in Sabha/Samiti; poets Apala, Vishwavara, Lopamudra; varna not rigid; crops: barley (yava), rice (vrhi/tandula/odana).
Later Vedic: Sati, child marriage prevalent; women's status declined; varna rigid (Brahmin-teach, Kshatriya-protect, Vaishya-trade, Shudra-serve); wheat (godhuma) introduced.
Early polity: King not absolute (janasya/gopa); cattle wealth (gomat); cow=aghnya; Sabha (elders) and Samiti (general) guide king; family=kula (kulapa), village=grama (gramani).
Later polity: King absolute; land wealth; imperialism; 16 Mahajanapadas; standing army (patti infantry, rathin cavalry); taxes: Bali, Bhaga, Shulka.
Early religion: nature gods (animism); Indra (250 hymns), Agni (200 hymns), Soma (120 hymns); no idol/temple worship; no afterlife belief.
Later religion: Indra/Agni decline; Brahma (creator), Rudra (destroyer), Vishnu (preserver); yajna sacrifices; goghna guests fed cattle products; yajamana performer; afterlife belief.
